doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Ali's father, records and Sundays without jazz
summary: Ali's father brought home Parker and Gillespie records, but jazz was not played on Sundays.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your father— what made him convert and leave that faith?

I don’t know what it was. You know like Philadelphia, it’s a very kind of a religious kind of place. Everybody’s looking for something different to be. You know. I mean they don’t want to be the same as this guy. They want to be different from that guy. So maybe that’s how it all went down. But whatever it was, it could have been the music too because he was definitely a person who listened to a lot of music. He used to, I mean he used to buy all the records and stuff in the house, so he had that stuff. He wasn’t a musician but he just listened. He brought in records from Bird and Billie Holiday and all that kind of stuff. Well my mom was the Billie Holiday person. He’d bring in Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie and people like that, and Bud Powell.
That’s just so interesting to me because Mom and Dad bringing home Charlie Parker.

Yeah music was played in my house all the time except Sundays, because my grandmother didn’t allow jazz to be played on Sundays in the house. You can play spiritual Gospel music, like Mahalia Jackson and Rosetta Tharpe and people like that, but you couldn’t play no Charlie Parker. Not on Sundays.
